name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Makes Proxy streaming mode actually take effect on items that already exist, which it never did. Reconciliation only ever created or deleted items - it never updated one - so the stream URL stamped on an item was frozen at the moment it was created. Switching a server to Proxy therefore changed nothing for every title already in the library: Jellyfin still served the stored Direct URL as a static media source *alongside* the freshly built Proxy one, listed it first, and clients played it. That is why switching modes repeatedly appeared to make no difference, and why streaming over a tunnel kept stalling - none of the Proxy relay's retry, idle-timeout and Range-resume handling was ever in the path. Reconciliation now restamps a stale URL in place. Deliberately an in-place update rather than the delete-and-recreate every earlier migration used, because deleting an item discards its watch progress and there is no reason to lose a resume point over a URL change. Verified live: 312 items restamped, after which the item served exactly one media source - the relay - with resume positions intact. Also documents the trap that hid this: Proxy needs the server's own URL, and syncing runs in the background with no incoming request to auto-detect one from, so leaving that field blank silently prevents the relay URL from ever being written. The field's hint now says so.
